content: Polycarbophil is a laxative that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of occasional constipation. It works to restore and maintain regular bowel movements. Typically, this medication induces a bowel movement within 12 to 72 hours after administration. Common side effects associated with its use include a sensation of fullness in the upper abdomen (epigastric fullness) and flatulence. For adults, the recommended dosage is to take each dose with at least 8 ounces (a full glass) of water or another fluid. Failure to consume sufficient liquid with this medication may result in choking. It is important to note that the product may require consistent use for one to three days to achieve its full therapeutic effect. The dosage may vary depending on factors such as diet, physical activity, prior use of laxatives, or the severity of constipation. There is limited information available regarding the use of Polycarbophil in pediatric patients, including both FDA-labeled and off-label uses. Similarly, there is no substantial data on its off-label use in adults. Polycarbophil carries a choking warning. If taken without adequate fluid, the product may swell and obstruct the throat or esophagus, potentially causing choking. Individuals with difficulty swallowing should not use this product. If symptoms such as chest pain, vomiting, difficulty swallowing, or difficulty breathing occur after taking the medication, immediate medical attention is required. Patients should consult a healthcare provider before using this product if they experience abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or a sudden change in bowel habits that persists for more than two weeks. Additionally, individuals taking other medications should consult a doctor or pharmacist, as Polycarbophil may interfere with the absorption or effectiveness of other drugs. It is recommended to take this product at least two hours before or after other medications. When using Polycarbophil, it should not be used for more than seven days unless directed by a healthcare provider. The maximum allowable dose is eight caplets within a 24-hour period unless otherwise instructed by a physician. If rectal bleeding occurs or if no bowel movement is achieved after using this or any other laxative, the patient should discontinue use and seek medical advice, as these symptoms may indicate a more serious condition. Polycarbophil should be kept out of the reach of children. In the event of an overdose, medical assistance or contact with a Poison Control Center should be sought immediately. There is limited information available regarding the clinical trial experience, postmarketing data, drug interactions, and specific population use of Polycarbophil. This includes its use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, nursing, pediatric and geriatric populations, and individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. There is also no specific guidance on its use in relation to gender, race, reproductive potential, or immunocompromised patients. Polycarbophil is administered orally. There is no information available regarding its intravenous use, monitoring requirements, IV compatibility, or overdose management. If overdose is suspected, the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) should be contacted immediately. The mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of Polycarbophil are not well-documented in the drug label. Similarly, there is limited information regarding clinical studies, storage conditions, and how the product is supplied. The interaction between alcohol and Polycarbophil has not been established. Patients should consult their healthcare provider regarding the potential effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication. Polycarbophil is marketed under the brand name FIBERCON®.
